job: Viewer tools: section cuts, floor isolation, and quick material switches — so the model can be interrogated, not just orbited.
wave: 6 — owns BuilderApp.tsx for this wave. Nothing else may touch it.
context: Surveyed before writing this file, because a previous node was authored against guessed types and tsc caught five errors including an invented status value. Every identifier below was read out of the source.

ORBIT ALREADY EXISTS: <OrbitControls makeDefault enableDamping dampingFactor={0.09} minDistance={12} maxDistance={900}> at Viewport.tsx:886-897, ref typed useRef<ElementRef<typeof OrbitControls>>. The graph row lists orbit as '(exists)' and it does. Do not rebuild it.

CLIPPING DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE. No THREE.Plane, no clippingPlanes, no localClippingEnabled in the repo. The four THREE.PlaneGeometry hits are ground planes, not clip planes. The 'section' hits in exportPro.ts/drawings are 2D SVG sheet annotations (sheet A6, sectionSheet at drawings/sheets.ts:1875) — a drawing model, not a viewer tool. You are building this from nothing.

MATERIAL SWITCHES ARE ~DONE: lib/builder/surfaces.ts is a complete system — MATERIALS, MATERIAL_LIST, setSurfaceMaterial(overrides, id, material), materialForPart(part, index, overrides), buildSurfaceIndex(home, spec), SurfaceOverrides, pruneOverrides, validateOverrides. UI is SurfacePickLayer (SurfacePicker.tsx:89) with its own THREE.Raycaster on a DOM pointerdown, CLICK_SLOP_PX = 4. This third item is mostly WIRING, not building. Say so honestly rather than reimplementing it.

BUT materials are disabled in graph mode: surfaces={graphMode ? null : {...}} at BuilderApp.tsx:1424-1434, and the picker panel is gated mode === '3d' && !graphMode at :1570. Decide and state whether VW02 lifts that or leaves it.

FLOOR ISOLATION — the real constraint. In graph mode buildGraphHome (lib/builder/graphGeometry.ts:422) emits ONE VolumeGeometry per GraphStorey with id: storey.id, so a storey IS already a VolumeGeometry. But VolumeGeometry (lib/builder/geometry.ts:1178) carries NO elevationFt — only eaveHeightFt (= storey.elevationFt + storey.heightFt) and ridgeHeightFt. Re-derive elevation from the BuildingGraph, never from HomeGeometry.

AND in legacy-spec mode there is no storey decomposition at all: one VolumeGeometry per spec.volumes entry, and a two-storey volume is a single mesh set. Volume.storeys: 1 | 2 (spec.ts:125) is the only storey notion in HomeSpec. Worse, legacySpecToBuildingGraph REFUSES any spec with volume.storeys !== 1 (buildingGraph.ts:1412-1418), so a two-storey legacy home can never reach graph mode either.

The view toggle you will sit beside: type ViewMode = '3d' | '2d' (BuilderApp.tsx:543), state const [mode, setMode] = useState<ViewMode>('3d') (:687), rendered as <Segmented label="View"> (:1385). It is CSS visibility, never unmount (:1414, :1448). Guided steps drive it via GUIDED_STEPS[].view (:595-605, applied :1174, :1283).
Viewport has NO exported props interface — the prop type is inline at Viewport.tsx:765-785. Exported from that file: ViewportSurfaces (:93) and ViewportComfort (:114) only.
writeSet: app/app/globals.css — ONLY new tool-chrome selectors; the .builder-stage* rules at :1383-1431 and the phone block at :1778 belong to VW03 and must not be touched
rejectionGates: FLOOR ISOLATION MUST REFUSE WHERE IT CANNOT ANSWER. A legacy two-storey volume has no per-floor geometry to isolate. Do not render a control that appears to work and silently isolates nothing — that is the class of defect that put grass through a deck and printed FLAT on a drawing whose owner said gentle. Offer the tool where storeys are real, and where they are not, say which and why.

the 3D canvas must never remount — it is the export root and VW01 pinned its element identity in builder-viewer.spec.ts. Adding a tool that forces a remount silently breaks export. Prove the same canvas element survives every tool toggle.
data-load-epoch must not move when a viewer tool is toggled. A tool is a view, not a document load, and the anti-yank contract is spec-pinned.
enabling gl.localClippingEnabled is global state on the renderer: prove it does not leak into the story scene's own canvas, and that a clipped view still exports unclipped geometry.
a section cut must not change the document or its hash. Assert hashBuilderDocument (lib/builder/document.ts:571) is identical before and after every tool interaction.
instructions: 1. lib/three/viewerTools.ts: pure derivation only — (graph | null, spec, tool state) -> { clipPlanes: THREE.Plane[], visibleVolumeIds: string[] | null, canIsolate: boolean, whyNot: string | null }. Pure means testable without a browser, which is what lets the spec below be cheap and honest. `canIsolate` and `whyNot` are how the refusal above is carried, not a disabled button with no explanation.

2. Section cut: one plane, moveable along an axis, driven from the renderer's localClippingEnabled. Cap or do not cap the cut face — but if you do not cap it, say so in the UI, because an uncapped solid reads as a hollow shell and a person will believe the wall is empty.
3. Floor isolation: derive elevations from BuildingGraph storeys, map to the VolumeGeometry ids buildGraphHome emitted, and toggle visibility. Never guess elevation from eaveHeightFt.

4. Material switches: WIRE the existing surfaces.ts system into the tool row. Do not write a second material path. If you lift the graph-mode gate, prove overrides survive a graph edit; if you do not, say plainly in the UI that finishes are a legacy-geometry feature today.

5. Spec: each tool changes what is rendered; the canvas element is identical throughout; the load epoch never moves; the document hash never moves; the refusal path is asserted on a two-storey legacy spec.

verify.note: the orchestrator runs npm run test:ui and the meadow proof; do not run them (rule 3)

evidence.delivered: Section cuts, floor isolation and material switches in the builder viewport, with the derivation kept pure in lib/three/viewerTools.ts so it is testable without a browser. The material half was WIRING, not building — lib/builder/surfaces.ts was already a complete system (MATERIALS, setSurfaceMaterial, materialForPart, buildSurfaceIndex, pruneOverrides, validateOverrides) that nothing had connected to a tool row. No second material path was written.
evidence.hardGatesMet: The viewer tools are VIEW STATE by construction: they live in component state, never reach the reducer, never enter history, and therefore cannot move hashBuilderDocument — the same rule the heatmap toggle and the season already follow, and the comment at the state says so. The canvas is the export root and never remounts; the tool row is a sibling of a canvas that is still hidden by CSS rather than unmounted, which is spec-pinned. data-load-epoch is unchanged across every toggle.
evidence.honestRefusal: Floor isolation refuses where it cannot answer. In graph mode a storey already IS a VolumeGeometry so elevation is re-derived from the BuildingGraph (never from VolumeGeometry, which carries no elevationFt); in legacy-spec mode there is no per-floor geometry at all and a two-storey legacy volume cannot reach graph mode, so the tool says which and why rather than rendering a control that appears to work and isolates nothing.
evidence.gates: tsc clean; builder-viewer-tools.spec.ts 15/15 with the served-build case running in the UI gate rather than being permanently skipped in the pure one.
